formalDefinition: Deutsch Jozsa = {(n, <w_1, w_2, ... , w_(2^n - 1), w_(2^n)> | n is int, w_i is bit (0 or 1)}
problemDefinition: Deutsch-Jozsa's algorithm solves the general case of the parity problem and therefore determines whether a function f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} is constant or balanced. It is represented by an ordered list of values, which show the functions output for the 2^n possible inputs.
inputDescription: f, a function {0,1}^n -> {0,1} promised to be constant or balanced, given as its truth table
outputDescription: Whether f is constant or balanced
source: Deutsch, David and Jozsa, Richard. 1992. Rapid solution of problems by quantum computation. Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A439553-558
instanceFormat: Format: {f | f is list} (f has 2^n bits, one output per input in {0,1}^n) Example: (1, 1, 1, 1)
certificateFormat: Format: 'constant' | f is constant, or 'balanced' | f is balanced Example: constant

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This solver classically solves the Deutsch-Jozsa problem by querying the oracle up to (n/2) + 1 times to determine if the function is constant or balanced.
defaultSolver.source: Deutsch, David and Jozsa, Richard. 1992. Rapid solution of problems by quantum computation. Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A439553-558

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This verifier uses the classical solver to verify the solution to the Deutsch-Jozsa problem.
defaultVerifier.source: Deutsch, David and Jozsa, Richard. 1992. Rapid solution of problems by quantum computation. Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A439553-558

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Requests the QASM for the Deutsch-Jozsa circuit (data qubits plus ancilla), showing the oracle and measurements that separate constant vs. balanced functions in one query for Q.js.
